name: bsnes-mercury (ASYNCIFY, dual profile)

asyncify.why: bsnes uses libco cooperative cothreads. In a plain single-threaded, non-ASYNCIFY WASM build retro_run never returns (the libco scheduler never yields back to JS), so the first frame hangs. Building with -s ASYNCIFY=1 lets retro_run unwind the Emscripten stack and RETURN to the browser event loop.
asyncify.libco_backend: Emscripten Fibers (libco/emscripten.c, added for the __EMSCRIPTEN__ target in libco/libco.c). ASYNCIFY alone is not enough because libco context-switches raw stacks ASYNCIFY does not know about; the Fibers backend (emscripten_fiber_*) makes cothread switches cooperate with ASYNCIFY.

accuracy.verified: run-smoke: retro_load_game true, retro_run returns (no hang), video_refresh non-null (512x224 XRGB8888), frame counter advances.

performance.verified: run-smoke: retro_load_game true, retro_run returns (no hang), video_refresh non-null (256x224 XRGB8888), frame counter advances.

output_note: Each profile is emitted with a DISTINCT filename AND a distinct MODULARIZE EXPORT_NAME (bsnes_accuracy / bsnes_performance) so the two cores never collide on a shared global/UMD symbol. Both are emitted as ES6 modules (-s EXPORT_ES6=1), so core-loader.js resolves either via the dynamic-import default export. The legacy snes9x_libretro name is kept in core-loader.js factoryNameGuesses only for backward compatibility with an older pre-ASYNCIFY core.
